messages:
maria (sec): Quick heads up — there's a PR to prune privileged caps from our base images (strip CAP_SYS_ADMIN, drop setuid, drop CAP_NET_RAW where possible). Before we merge, we need a short safety checklist: RBAC changes needed for builders/signers, KMS signing access, mapping audit logs to workloads, and a fallback/rollback plan. Who's available to triage?
praveen (infra): On it. First question: do we have an inventory of workloads that explicitly request capabilities? If we don't, we should discover them before hard-blocking. :mag: I can run a cluster scan but need a quick command suggestion.
liam (eng-runtime): You can start with this one-liner to list pods with non-empty securityContext.capabilities.add:``` 
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}:{.metadata.name} {.spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.add}\n{end}' | grep -v "<none>"
```That will catch most. For init containers, run same against .spec.initContainers.
jess (platform): Also check images that use setuid binaries (busybox, sudo shims). I have a quick container scan image that looks for suid bits and file capabilities — can run as a DaemonSet in dev first.
anita (eng-sre): From rollout perspective, we should gate this with an admission controller that audits first, then denies. OPA/Gatekeeper policy idea below. We keep it audit mode for one week, then deny on day X. Minimal policy snippet:```
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sprivcaps
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sPrivCaps
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sprivcaps
      deny[msg] {
        some i
        caps := input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.capabilities.add
        caps[_] == "CAP_NET_ADMIN"
        msg = "CAP_NET_ADMIN is disallowed by policy"
      }
```We can roll this in audit-only mode first.
praveen (infra): Good. On RBAC/KMS: cosign will need a principal for signing. Do we want a single org-wide KMS key or per-team keys? Org key is simpler but higher blast radius. If per-team, we need clear IAM bindings. Proposed least-priv: service account with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySigner for the key and no storage perms. Audit logs must sink to security project.
maria (sec): Prefer per-team keys for blast-radius. Also need to ensure signing operations are logged and the logs include the image name + digest and the build/request principal. That requires the signing service to annotate the audit entry — please confirm possible.
liam (eng-runtime): GCP KMS + Cloud Audit Logs will show the signer principal and operation. We can augment the build pipeline to emit structured log: {image:, digest:, builder_sa:, cosign_key_id:}. Those logs should be forwarded to our SIEM. For cosign using KMS, the signing command looks like:```
COSIGN_PASSWORD="" cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/REDACTED/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/key@1 image:sha256:... 
```Note: provide SA credentials via workload identity or short-lived token, not long-lived key.
jess (platform): We'll need a small RBAC ticket: grant the build runners the cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter? Wait for signing only we need cryptoKeySign. I'll draft the IAM bindings and a terraform snippet.
praveen (infra): Also: check KMS audit configuration — we must enable Data Access audit logs for the key (they are disabled by default). If not enabled, sign events won't be visible in the audit sink.
anita (eng-sre): For runtime fallback: plan to publish both signed and unsigned images during canary window and have the admission controller accept unsigned images from a specific canary namespace only. Rollout plan: 1) inventory (praveen) 2) admission audit + alerting (anita) 3) create per-team KMS keys + IAM (jess/praveen) 4) canary rebuild with signed images (liam) 5) full deny enforcement after 1 week canary (maria).
rebuild-bot: Scheduled: base-image rebuild window queued for 2024-11-05T02:00:00Z. Owners notified.
maria (sec): Minor ops Q — do we need to rotate cosign key on rebase? Like key versioning strategy? I think rotate after every major rebase or quarterly, but want ops input.
liam (eng-runtime): Key rotation: prefer key versioning (KMS supports versions). Re-sign important images on rotation; have rebuild job detect key version mismatch and re-sign. We can automate a 'resign' job.
jess (platform): I'll create TF for per-team KMS keys + grant cryptoKeySign to build SA and logging sink. Will post PR for review.
praveen (infra): I'll run the cluster scan today and post a list. If anyone has a short-lived script request (e.g., include initContainers, hostPID, hostNetwork), ping me.
anita (eng-sre): I'll stand up the Gatekeeper audit policy in staging and add alerts to the sec-runbook for findings. If we get >5 denies in 24h, pause and investigate.
maria (sec): Plan looks good. Taking ownership of final enforcement decision and incident playbook. Quick action items: - praveen: inventory by EOD - jess: KMS TF PR by tomorrow - liam: canary resign script - anita: audit policy to staging - everyone: watch the rebuild window notice. :thumbsup:
praveen (infra): Filing SEC ticket SEC-482 and attaching inventory task. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-482
